chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: In this section we are going to cover how to change the flow of the code in Python.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: For example, imagine you have some code that you only want to run if a certain value is true.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Or maybe you want to repeat i.e. loop a code as long as the condition is true.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Finally, maybe you want to run some code for every entry inside of a container like a list or a tuple.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: For all of that we are going to cover some logic in this video.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: And the most important thing we have to learn about is a boolean value.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: This is a new data type that can only be true or false.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: There is no other value possible.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: The easiest way to create it is with comparison operators,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: like equal to, smaller than or greater than.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Notice for this one we are using two equal signs to check for equality,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: since a single equal sign assigns a value to a variable.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Let's play around with all of that first of all, just to have some basic idea of what's going on.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Once again we are back in the code and I want to create a new Python file, let's call it flow.py.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Then I can go into fullscreen again.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: And now I want to create a basic boolean value.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: The easiest way of doing that is I want to print some kind of comparison.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Let's say 5 is equal to 5.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: If I run that code, we are getting the output true.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Which seems like the correct result for this one.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: However, if I change this to a 4,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: then we are getting false, because 5 is different from 4.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: However, what you could be checking is if 5 is greater than 4,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: then we get true once again.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: So the result of this operation would be a boolean value.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Which we can use.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: For example, imagine we only want to run some code if this kind of condition is true.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: For that we have an if statement.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Which is going to look for a boolean value.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: For example we could add in 5 is greater than 4, which would be true.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: And now pay close attention.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: If I press enter, Python indents the line by one tap.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: And this is really important.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Let me add one line for now.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: I want to print correct result.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: With the print statement being indented.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: This indentation is really important.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Because it tells Python that this print belongs to this if statement.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: If it wasn't indented, Python would consider it as a general part of the code.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Meaning it would run regardless of the result of the if statement.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: As a matter of fact, let me add another print statement that is not indented.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: So print, let's say test.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: If I now run the code, we can see the correct result.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: This is what we get from this print statement.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: And then we get test, which is the second print statement.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: The first print statement, the one with correct result, only ran because this if condition is true.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: If it wasn't true, let's say we can change this to 5 is equal to 4 and run the code again.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Then we cannot see the print correct result.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Because the if statement is false.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: However, we can see test.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Because this one is not indented, so it's not part of the if statement.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: So I hope that makes sense.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: But if you get the basic idea, you understand basic if statements.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: We add the if keyword, then we add some kind of boolean value.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: This can either be a boolean value directly.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: So if you add if false, this is never going to run.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: And if you add if true, it is always going to run.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: But most of the time you have some kind of comparison.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Let's say 5 is greater than 4.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: And then it would be running.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: On top of that, what you can also do is add an else statement.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Let's say we can have print correct result and print incorrect result.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: If I now run the code, we're getting the correct result.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Because the first if statement ran.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: However, if we change the condition, let's say 3 is greater than 4, and run this again,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: we're getting the incorrect result.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Since the condition was false, we're running the else statement.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: And that way we're getting the incorrect result.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: And once again, the print statement for incorrect result is indented,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: so Python knows it's part of the else bit.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: What you can also do is add an elif statement.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: The way it works is we first of all check if a condition is true.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: At the moment, this one would not be correct.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Then we can check for another condition.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Let's say 2 is greater than 1.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: And if that is the case, we need a double colon again.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: We can print, let's say, some other result.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Which in this case would run because 2 is indeed greater than 1.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: However, if that wasn't the case, we would go to else.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Let me run all of this.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: We're getting some other result.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Because for the elif statement, the condition is true.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: If it wasn't, let's say 0 is greater than 1,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: we would simply end up with the incorrect result.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: You can expand this system quite a bit.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: For example, you could have multiple elif statements.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Let me duplicate it and add it like so.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: We can for example check if 0 is equal to 0.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: And this one would be true, so we're getting some other result.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: The if statement would end on this bit.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: You can also chain different parts together inside of an if statement.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Meaning we only want to for example run this elif statement,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: if 0 is 0, and let's say 5 is greater than 1.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Only if both of these values are true,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: then we are going to run this elif statement.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: And something like this could be done for every single if statement.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Also, what you could be doing,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: inside of any of these if statements,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: add another nested if statement.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: I could add if and then add another condition.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: And you can be quite fancy with your conditions.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: For example, what you could be checking is the length of some list

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: with 1, 2 and 3.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: If that list is greater than 2,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: then we want to do something else.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Let's say print list is long enough.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: And now if I run the code again,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: we get some other result,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: because this condition and this condition is correct.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: So we are printing this bit,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: and then we are running the other if statement,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: and we are getting to this print statement.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: I think the logic for all of this is fairly straightforward.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: There isn't that much to it.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: The main thing you have to understand is that you always need an if statement,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: then a condition,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: and then you want to indent whatever code you want to run by one tap.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: The code you can add is basically whatever you want.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Could even be another if statement,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: or some function, or method, or list, or dictionary.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Literally whatever you want.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Python is super flexible.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: And well, with that, we have if.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: That is basically all you have to know about them.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Next up, we have a while loop.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: This one is going to run a code

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: as long as a certain condition is true.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: And to work with all of that,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: I am going to comment out all the things we have done for the if statement.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: For example, what we could be doing is,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: first of all, I want to have some kind of counter,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: which is starting at 0.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: And then I am going to use the while keyword.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: This one, like if, wants to have some kind of condition.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: For example, let's say that the counter is smaller than 10.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Or to use a comparison we haven't used yet,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: smaller or equal to 10.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: If that is the case, we want to print,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: let's say we want to print the counter.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: And after that, we want to increase the counter by 1.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Now, if I run this again,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: we are getting numbers from 0 all the way to 10,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: and then the while loop stops.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: We are checking this condition,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: and as long as counter is below or equal to 10,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: we are running the code inside of it,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: which is going to print the number,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: and then increase counter by 1,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: which is going to run 10 times from 0 all the way to 10,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: and then it stops.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Or rather, we go to the line after the while loop.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: And there we can print,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: while loop has finished.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Now let me print it again,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: and we get at the end, while loop has finished.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Once again, the indentation is really important.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: This print statement and this counter

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: are part of the while loop,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: because of the indentation.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Indenting things in Python is fundamental.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: That way you know a line of code belongs to an if statement,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: a while loop,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: or later to something like a function or a class.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Also, what you could be doing in there,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: is add an if statement,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: so if counter is equal to 5,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: then I want to print,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: I don't know, counter is 5.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: If I now run this again,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: we can see on number 5,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: counter is 5.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: And if I had spelled this correctly,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: this would also look much better.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: But anyway, you know it's working perfectly well.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: And that is basically all you have to know about while loops.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: They are honestly not that common in Python.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Also, you really want to be careful with them,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: because if you mess up,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: this while loop is going to run forever.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: And might crash your code.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: For example, if you forgot to add this counter plus 1,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: let me comment it out actually.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: And now run the code.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: It is going to run forever.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: We are getting a 0 eternally.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: We are never going to reach this print statement,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: or any code we had after this while loop.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: If you ever ended up in an infinite loading screen,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: this is what might have happened.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: So be careful when you are using while loops.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: You always want to have some kind of escape condition.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Which in our case is the counter plus equal 1.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: But that's about it.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: While loops aren't that complicated.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Finally, we have a for loop.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: A for loop is similar to a while loop.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Except that this one is only working for every single entry

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: of some kind of container.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Let me create a test list.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Which is going to be a list with 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: The way a for loop works is with the for keyword.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: And then we need a certain kind of name.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Let me for now say,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: for x in test list.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: What is going to happen,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: is that Python is going to go through every single item

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: inside of the test list.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Meaning 1, 2, 3 and so on in our case.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: And then on every single loop,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: it is going to store that value inside of this x.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Or whatever you name the value.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Basically, we are creating a variable

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: for the duration of this for loop.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: And storing the current item we are looking at

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: inside of this variable.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: That way we can easily use it inside of this for loop.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: For example, we can print x.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: If I run the code now,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: we are getting the values from 1 to 5.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Exactly what I have specified inside of the list.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Also, if you are only seeing zeros in the terminal,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: then the while loop is still running for you.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: To end that one, simply press on the trash can symbol.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: That way you are ending the code.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: And then run everything again.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: It should work just fine.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Cool. But in our case, we have a simple for loop.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Where we can execute some code

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: for every single item inside of any kind of container.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: This is going to work with a list, a tuple, a set and a dictionary.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: In fact, let me create a set really quick

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: with 1, 2, 3 and 3.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: And once again, we are getting the values from 1 to 3.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Remember, a set ignores any duplicate values.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Then we can have a tuple with 1, 2, 3 and 3.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: And then we are getting all of those values.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: And if we have a dictionary

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: with a couple of key value pairs,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: let's say 1 and 2,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: then we have 3 and 4,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: and we have 5 and 6.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: If I now run it, we only get 1, 3 and 5.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Which are all of the keys of the dictionary.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Which is not necessarily what you want to get.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: For that, inside of a for loop.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Especially for a dictionary,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: you have a couple of methods that are super useful.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Those would be keys, and don't forget to call this one.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: And this one would only return the keys of the dictionary.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Meaning if I run this again,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: we are getting the same outcome,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: because this is the default value.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: However, what you can be doing is values.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: That way, you are getting only the values.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: And on top of that, there is one more method called items.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: And this one is returning both.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Meaning we are getting a tuple with the key value pairs.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: And then we have access to the entirety of the dictionary

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: inside of one for loop.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: But other than that, you can still run whatever code you want

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: inside of the for loop.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: In that regard, it's very similar compared to while or if.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: So not that much new stuff to learn.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: For example, what you could be doing,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: for this x, you could use indexing.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Where we only want to get the first item.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Then I can print this again.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: And now we are back to only getting the keys of the dictionary.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: I suppose there is one more thing that you do want to be aware of

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: with a for loop.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: And that is that at the moment,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: we are always getting a key value pair inside of a tuple.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Meaning we have a tuple with always two items.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Since this is a bit annoying to work with,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: with a single variable,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Python has a nice feature.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Where if you know the length of the tuples you are getting returned,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: or more generally, if you have any kind of data structure,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: where you know the amount of items inside of the container,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: then you can unpack the items right away.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: In my case, I know I always get a key and a value.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: k and v for short.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: I can unpack both of them right away inside of the for loop.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: That way, inside of the loop,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: I can get access to the values much more easily.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: I can print k and v,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: and the result would be that I have access to the values individually.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Especially for more complex for loops,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: this kind of system can be really handy to work with.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: But alright, with that,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: we have the three major tools that you can use to control the flow of the code.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: And also you can combine them.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Now, before we go to an exercise,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: there's one more really important concept that I want to cover.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: So far, we only used the basic comparison operators.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: But in Python, you have another concept,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: which is called truthy or falsy,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: which are the result of an automatic conversion of any data type to a boolean.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: So what does that mean?

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Well, basically in Python,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: every empty container,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: every string without a letter,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: and every zero is going to evaluate to false.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Everything else is going to be truthy.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: If you add a zero into an if statement,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Python needs to figure out what it's going to do.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: And for that, we have truthy and falsy,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: where a zero inside of an if statement is going to be a false value,

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: or it's going to be the equivalent of a false value.

chunks.title: Control Flow
chunks.text: Let's play around with that really quick.
